math_notes: Extremely math-dense: full derivation of the variational lower bound, KL-divergence terms, Gaussian transition kernels, noise schedules (beta_t, alpha_t), and a simplified L_simple training loss, concentrated especially in section 3 and Appendix A. Multi-line/stacked equations and subscripted process-indexing notation (L_T, L_1:T-1, L_0) appear inside section HEADINGS themselves (e.g. '3.1 Forward process and L_T') -- this is a specifically interesting stress case: a heading-detector that strips 'non-alphanumeric' characters aggressively could mangle these headings, and a math-detector scanning heading text could misfire on headings that are legitimately headings, not equations.

notes_for_implementer: Like fixture 01, this is a clean two-column LaTeX PDF -- included as a second, MORE math-heavy native-PDF data point precisely because several section headings themselves contain mathematical notation (L_T, L_1:T-1, L_0). This directly probes the boundary between 'math notation detector' and 'heading detector': Pith should still recognize '3.1 Forward process and L_T' as a heading (not as a stray equation), while independently flagging the genuine equation blocks in the body text as math. Appendices A-D use letter-numbering instead of digit-numbering, which is a useful check that the heading-numbering heuristic isn't hardcoded to digits only.
